questions.question: AGMT is related to GMSZ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, YEKR is related to EKQX. To which of the following is QWCJ related, following the same logic?

What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged, and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

11 ÷ 3 + 30 × 6 − 12 = ?

This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.(Left)      574      249      592      746      240      (Right)(Example: 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)(Note: All operations to be done from left to right.)What will be the resultant if the first digit of the second highest number is multiplied with the second digit of the lowest number?

Given below is a statement followed by two possible reasons numbered I and II. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the two reasons explains the event/observation/information given in the statement. Statement:The new smartphone model R from Company A, despite its advanced features and competitive pricing, did not achieve robust sales in the market.Reasons:I: Company A launched the smartphone R during the holiday season, when consumer spending is at its peak.II: Company A had to recall its earlier smartphone model in large numbers because of a battery fault, which garnered significant media attention.
options: Only I is a possible reason.
Neither I nor II is a possible reason.
Both I and II are possible reasons.
Only II is a possible reason.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (Only II is a possible reason.) है।

questions.question: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? MAN  KYL  IWJ  GUH  ?

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.Statements: All shoes are blankets.All pies are logs.No pies are blankets.Conclusions:(I) No logs are blankets.(II) No shoes are pies.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'D' (Only conclusion (II) follows.) है।

Avneet starts from Point Y and drives 38 km towards east. He then takes a right turn, drives 12 km, turns right and drives 17 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 55 km. He takes a left turn and drives 21 km. He then turns left and drives 29 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only, unless specified.)
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (14 km towards south) है।

questions.question: In a certain code language, ‘HOPE’ is coded as ‘7416’ and ‘POLE’ is coded as ‘1367’. What is the code for ‘L’ in the given code language?

Each of P, O, I, U, Y, T and R has an exam on a different day of a week, starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. T has an exam on Friday. Only two people have exams between R and O. Only three people have exams between R and T. P has an exam immediately before I. P doesn’t have an exam on Tuesday. How many people have exams before I and after R?

Similarly, certain mathematical operation on the second number results in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the question?(Note: A two-/three-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits for operations e.g., if 37 is followed by 10, the operation cannot be 3 + 7 as a two-digit number cannot be broken into individual digits.) 84-104-129-159; 77-97-122-152

Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Karl is an immediate neighbour of both Pamela and Nadia. Laura is sitting second to the left of Pamela. Milo is sitting third to the right of Nadia. Olin is an immediate neighbour of both Laura and Nadia. The position(s) of how many persons will remain unchanged if all persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order, in clockwise direction, starting from Karl (including Karl)?

Only three people have exams between X and Z. Only three people have exams between V and C. B has an exam immediately before N. How many people have exams between M and N?
